newsitem.title: USA: One tax limitation measure makes Nebraska ballot.
newsitem.headline: One tax limitation measure makes Nebraska ballot.

text.p: Only one proposed constitutional amendment aimed at limiting property taxes in Nebraska will be on the Nov 5 ballot, according to Secretary of State Scott Moore.

Moore said Friday he certified that enough valid signatures had been collected for a petition drive by the state's education association and farm bureau to limit local property taxes, while guaranteeing a quality education for students.
A second proposed constitutional amendment aimed at wiping out all local property taxes was not certified for the ballot, Moore added.
Backers of the measures had filed enough signatures on petitions by a July deadline for consideration for the ballot.
Moore said the constitutional question that made the ballot has been split into two parts.

Under one question, the legislature would be directed to devise a way to determine fair market value of real estate for property tax purposes within certain limitations and establish "standards of efficiency" for local government delivery of services.

The second question would ask voters if Nebraska's constitution should be amended to include quality education as a fundamental right and a "paramount duty" of the state. The legislature would also be directed to create a school financing system that among other things would provide per pupil funding for the 1998-99 school year that is at least equal to funding in the 1997-98 school year.

In an unsuccessful effort to stop the petition drives, the Nebraska Legislature in April passed a two percent cap on local government budget increases in fiscal 1997 and a limit on their property tax levies starting in 1999.

The legislature's action sparked concerns by Moody's Investors Service, which issued a comment in April that said the limitations "may adversely affect local government financial performance, raising concerns for long-term credit quality."
